transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-05-17 15:00 UTC; Duration: ~52 minutes; Recorded with Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nia Gomez (Redwood SE), Jamie Lin (Coastal - Head of ML), Priya Rao (Coastal - CTO), Ethan Park (Coastal - Finance PM), Ravi Desai (Coastal - Platform)

Summary: High level qualification on per-token economics, batching and cache levers; preliminary pilot scope; security and VPC constraints discussed. Customer wants clear hosted vs dedicated vs private run-rate and SLOs.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros real quick, then we'll dive into cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:18] Jamie (Coastal - Head of ML): Hi all, Jamie here. we're trying to understand what it looks like to move our chat summarization and realtime suggestions from a homegrown cluster -> to Redwood. main constraints are monthly budget cap ~ $45k and p95 latency target around 400ms for short prompts.
[00:35] Priya (CTO): we also need to check VPC/networking and encryption, we have strict residency rules for some PII-ish fields.
[00:45] Alex: great. Samir, want to take the econ framing?
[00:48] Samir (Redwood SE): yeah, quick frame. Redwood has three common paths: hosted (pay-for-what-you-use), dedicated reserved GPU pools, or private (VPC/on-prem). On per-token math, hosted is simplest — example ballpark numbers we usually quote are on the order of "mid-microunits" per token depending on model; dedicated moves you towards a fixed monthly footprint and lower marginal token cost but requires capacity commit.
[01:15] Ethan (Finance): can you be a bit more specific on the "mid-micro"? our FP&A needs numbers to run runway.
[01:22] Samir: sure, for a 1k-2k token generation average we often see per-request costs convert to roughly $0.0005-0.001 per token on hosted for the models we surface; with dedicated those can drop by 30-60% depending on utilization, batching, and quantization choices. these are ballpark; we'll send a spreadsheet with scenarios.
[01:45] Jamie: okay that's useful. what does batching actually buy us in practice? we can't always batch long tail user requests.
[01:52] Nia (Redwood SE): good q. continuous batching helps for high QPS steady streams — you get throughput so per-token GPU amortization improves. practically for our customers we've seen 1.5-3x reductions in token-cost depending on sequence lengths and how much prefix reuse you have. important: caching (KV/prefix cache) can reduce effective tokens by avoiding re-sending the same prompt context. for example, for our suggestion flow where the first 40 tokens are repeated, KV caching reduced token footprint by ~25-40% in one pilot.
[02:20] Ravi (Platform): when you say KV cache, do you mean we need to run a separate cache node or it's managed? and does that affect private vs hosted?
[02:28] Samir: Redwood manages KV cache in hosted; on Dedicated it's an option we operate inside your reserved pool; for Private (VPC/on-prem) we provide an operator and config; but there's some extra ops for housekeeping. also, cache behavior depends on your conversational pattern — if you have short-lived sessions it's less effective.
[02:45] Priya: security checklist — SOC2, SAML, KMS — can you confirm Redwood has these? also audit logs and retention?
[02:53] Alex: yes, we have SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO and RBAC, KMS integrations, and per-request audit logs for Dedicated/Private with configurable retention. we'll share the security packet.
[03:05] Ethan: From finance perspective, what's the typical commit / term for Dedicated? we prefer quarterly but open to annual if the math makes sense.
[03:12] Samir: Dedicated typically has monthly or annual reserved capacity contracts. the deeper the commit, the better the unit economics. we can model a 6- or 12-month pilot where you reserve a smaller pool then scale to full commit.
[03:25] Jamie: timeline question — we want a pilot in prod-like traffic in 3 weeks. is that feasible?
[03:30] Alex: yes, feasible. pilot scope commonly: 2-4 endpoints, subset of traffic (10-20%), run 2 weeks for steady stats. we do a perf baseline then tune batching/cache.
[03:40] Nia: for the pilot we'll want a sample prompt set and traffic distribution. even a single day's log helps size buckets.
[03:48] Ravi: ops question — on Dedicated, how are fallbacks handled when capacity is saturated? do requests queue or do you failover to hosted?
[03:55] Samir: policy-based routing. you can set fallbacks: queue with graceful degradation, route to a cheaper model variant, or failover to hosted public pool. for critical user flows we recommend setting a per-route fallback to a smaller model first and then hosted only if needed.
[04:10] Jamie: do you have examples of cost delta for fallback combos? e.g., heavy fallbacks to hosted nucleus cost spikes?
[04:17] Samir: yes, that's important. if your dedicated pool is saturated and you route to hosted, your marginal per-token cost can jump — so in our cost model we simulate saturation events and show 95th percentile cost under different fallback policies.
[04:30] Ethan: pricing leakage is our fear — if we cap spend we need hard ceilings. can Redwood enforce a billing cap?
[04:36] Alex: we can set quota guards and automated routing to throttle or block; for Hosted we recommend quotas on API keys; for Dedicated we can apply pool-level autoscale guards and burst limits. we also provide alerting when spend approaches thresholds.
[04:50] Jamie: on residency and PII — some prompts must never leave our VPC or be logged externally. which mode supports that?
[04:57] Alex: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) gives you control — control plane still does management but you can airgap tokens and use customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated adds isolation but note that the control plane might be managed; we'll surface options for strict requirements.
[05:10] Priya: procurement timeline -- legal will want a DPA + CLA. Also, indemnity and data residency clauses matter.
[05:17] Alex: we'll loop in legal and share our standard DPA and enterprise terms.

--- Technical deep dive section (Samir leads) ---

[05:40] Samir: quick sketch of the per-token math: total cost = (model compute token cost + infra amortization + cache miss overhead + routing/fallback premium) / effective tokens. Key levers: batching factor, percent cache hits, model quantization variant, and utilization %. Example: 60% utilization on a dedicated fleet with 2x batching and 30% cache hit can cut per-token by ~45% vs baseline hosted.
[06:25] Ravi: what about cold-start KV cache effects? will first requests spike cost?
[06:32] Nia: yes, initial cold-start can increase cost; we recommend warmup phases in pilot and TTL tuning. we also support sticky routing to keep working sets local to reduce evictions.
[06:45] Jamie: are there tradeoffs to quantization on quality? our quality bar is high for summarization.
[06:50] Samir: small model variants and extreme quantization can affect some tasks; we run eval suites on your prompt set as part of the pilot to quantify quality delta. often 4-bit quantization is acceptable with little degradation for many tasks but we validate.

[07:15] Ethan: finance wants a 12-month projection if we go dedicated — can Redwood provide NPV-ish analysis comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[07:22] Alex: yes, we'll produce a projection with sensitivity bands (utilization +/-20%, billing spikes due to fallbacks).

[07:40] Jamie: internal stakeholders? procurement and security are critical; if we get a good pilot, procurement wants a 60-90 day window to sign main contract.
[07:50] Priya: also need a slide pack for execs showing risk, cost savings, and SLA.
[07:55] Alex: we'll include an exec one-pager in the follow-up.

[08:10] Samir: quick note on observability: Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost, per-route latency, and traces. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your datadog/stackdriver.
[08:25] Ravi: will logs contain prompt text? we need redaction options.
[08:30] Nia: yes, we support configurable redaction and event sampling; for Private you control retention.

[09:00] (discussion of a small benchmark they ran)
[09:10] Jamie: we ran some internal tests on 2x A100 nodes, p95 was ~380ms for short prompts but the cost was hard to pin because of ops overhead. we want to see if Redwood lowers ops burden and cost.
[09:22] Samir: that'll be the focus of the pilot: we reproduce your baseline and then show per-token delta with batching/cache on/off and hosted vs dedicated.

[12:15] (longer discussion about sample traffic and token distributions, customer shares numbers verbally)

[20:00] Ethan: one wrinkle — we have a hard budget cap for Q3 of $45k; if we go live sooner we need to ensure we don't blow through it in first month. how do teams usually control for that?
[20:12] Alex: we recommend a phased rollout with quotas and a throttling policy; also use route-level rewrite to send low-risk features to smaller models. our cost model will include a month-1 worst-case scenario.
[20:30] Priya: can the pilot be billed as a separate cost center so procurement can see exact spend?
[20:35] Alex: yes, we can separate billing and provide cost allocation tags and invoices per project.

[28:00] (narrow technical questions about network egress and VPC peering)
[28:15] Ravi: if we do Private in our VPC, what traffic egress do we still have to allow?
[28:22] Nia: for Private, most traffic stays in your VPC. control-plane calls can be optionally turned off for full air-gap but that requires an on-prem package and longer lead time.

[33:00] (discussion of SLA numbers)
[33:10] Jamie: what's the SLA for p95 latency on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[33:15] Samir: Hosted has best-effort latency; we provide SLOs on latency for higher tiers. Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets that we can codify per contract. we'll propose targets matching your 400ms p95 goal in the follow up and show how different model sizes and batching affect that.

[40:05] Ethan: any gotchas on billing reconciliation? how granular are invoices?
[40:10] Alex: invoices can be per-token and per-hour buckets; we include detailed line items per route and model. we provide monthly and real-time usage dashboards.

[45:22] (customer asks for a concrete worked example)
[45:30] Samir: Suppose you serve 3M tokens/week, with average generation 800 tokens, 20% cache hit, batching factor of 1.8; for hosted that maps to X per-month. With dedicated (50% utilization to start) the per-token drops and with improved batching at 2.5 and 35% cache hit you could see a 40% cost reduction vs hosted. we'll build exact numbers in the spreadsheet using your traffic.

[48:50] Jamie: awesome. last question: where do errors show up in the console? we need to debug mispredictions quickly.
[48:58] Nia: we provide per-request traces and sampling of inputs with optional PII redaction; you can hook tracing to your Sentry/datadog.

[50:10] Alex: recap and next steps — we'll share: 1) security + SOC2 packet and standard DPA, 2) tailored cost model spreadsheet with hosted/dedicated/private scenarios, 3) pilot runbook and sizing template, 4) exec one-pager and SLA draft. Samir will set up pilot kickoff with Ravi.
[50:30] Priya: ok that's great, please include clear conservative and optimistic spend paths.
[50:38] Ethan: thanks, looking forward to the spreadsheet.
[50:40] Alex: we'll aim to have the cost model and docs to you by 2026-05-20.
[51:00] (meeting wraps, casual sign-offs)

References mentioned: security packet link (shared after meeting), pilot runbook template (to be shared), cost spreadsheet (to be shared), internal benchmark note (Coastal provided sample logs).

Notes on transcription: occasional misheard acronyms, some crosstalk; timestamps approximate.
